image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) resting on a grassy surface with a textured stone wall in the background. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a brown chest, and greyish-brown body plumage. Its bill is yellow-green with a dark tip. The legs and feet are not visible as the bird is in a tucked, resting posture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with the correct yellow-green coloration and dark tip typical of a mallard drake.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is compact and rounded, typical of a resting waterfowl. The plumage appears dense and smooth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brown/grey body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is in a resting/tucked position; the legs and feet are completely occluded by the body and grass.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing the correct contour and feather layering for a broad, pointed wing structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the duck shows the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers).
